title: Is it common now to use AI for almost all the game development?
author: Able_Tell9927
selftext:
I worked as a backend developer before, and now I am a product manager.    
I always wanted to make my own game, but before AI, making a game alone was really painful and frustrating for me. There are too many things need to learn and handle, like coding, framework, bugs, UI, art and game design.    
Now AI agents are getting much stronger. I feel like I finally have a chance to make a game by myself, but work a little bit like a small team.    
I just started my first indie game. It is a factory simulator, and now I am still working on the basic prototype.    
So I want to ask, is it common now for indie developers to use AI during almost the whole development process?    
And for me, as a person with ADHD, this way also helps me keep moving and not give up so easily.

comments.author: Roma2443
comments.body: There is no dev working without AI

replies.author: Yamhar
replies.body: There is, but everyday it’s getting more rare to come by

replies.author: Queasy-Form-4261
replies.body: Yea there is. And they will be unemployed like the construction worker that still dig holes with their hands instead of a backhoe.  No one's waiting 5 months for you to dig a hole when the other guy can use a backhoe and have it done in 5 minutes.

replies.author: Yamhar
replies.body:
Some people just do it for a fun hobby and don’t use AI because they find learning it themselves more fun. (Me lol)

Not everyone’s in a race to become a mega rich game developer.

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
all the pro game devs are using AI tools to one degree or another. 

They aren't just text-2-imaging though. 

Ai becomes part of an already existing workflow but doesn't replace all steps in the workflow. 

It becomes another tool alongside many traditional media production tools.

replies.author: PomegranateIcy1614
replies.body: citation?

replies.author: Able_Tell9927
replies.body:
Yes, AI can help me a lot with gameplay and game design, but I still haven’t decided whether I want to use AI for the art. I feel there are some risks, and the results are not always that good.  
Also, I’m still working on the prototype now, so I haven’t really started the art part yet. And honestly, I’m not very good at art myself.

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body:
You can use it as prototype/place holders until you can came up witj something better.

If its 3d creation tripo, meshy rodin, hunyuan etc are better than just ChatGPT or Claude for the graphics.

replies.author: bigorangemachine
replies.body:
AI development is good for a proof of concept.

The issue is the code is hard to scale.  So if you learning how to program and you are using AI... you gonna have a bad time.

AI still needs you to have some skill & understanding of concepts.

replies.author: Easy-Coconut-33
replies.body: I use trellis through Python. It using my graphic card to make 3D models. It want 24 gb but there is a GitHub plugin that lowers that to 12gb. Rly good imo.

replies.author: TheClangers
replies.body:
This is not entirely true.

I work in AAA co-development and we're only just starting to see studios rolling out broad use of AI and only in engineering or early art ideation.

There are a couple of projects I've seen in this space that are using it for art more specifically with interesting purposes but otherwise it's mostly to speed up code.

replies.author: arscene
replies.body:
I work at an indie studio and I'd say it is used to:
- localize text
- brainstorm
- some code (almost nothing in production, a lot in prototypes)

Things that have already been done and can be found as package or add-ons, we buy them. It's nice to have pieces that do the heavy lifting without having to maintain them yourself.

Other than that we already have workflows.

replies.author: tcpukl
replies.body:
You could literally be working at the same studio as me. It's being used massively as a tool. Zero vibe coding. MCP bring used more as well as a technical tool in the editor.

But still zero creative make this shit. 

Only ever a tool for efficiency.

comments.author: Able_Tell9927
comments.body:
Some people say they would rather play a rough game made by humans. I think maybe they have never tried developing a game alone.  
When you are a solo developer, you have to deal with technical problems, performance, data design, and many other things that are not really about the gameplay itself. It’s very easy to lose patience during the process.

comments.author: fued
comments.body:
Its easy to make a game fully with AI.

But it will make what you tell it. And most people aren't an art director, a code architect, a UI expert, a gameplay designer, a play experience designer and an audio expert all in one.

So it makes slop

replies.author: Able_Tell9927
replies.body:
I understand. Things like how you structure and store data, or even how you implement a feature, can affect future iteration and scalability.  
But honestly, for someone like me who knows a little bit about everything but isn’t really an expert at anything, and is also kind of lazy, AI is a huge help.

replies.author: fued
replies.body: Programming is probably the least important. Gameplay experience, UI and art direction are the three most tbh

replies.author: Able_Tell9927
replies.body: **I’m making a simulator game about a fabric dyeing factory, so the logic is also very important for my game. I agree that UX and art are important, but they are not my strong points.**

replies.author: Able_Tell9927
replies.body: I will keep learning.

replies.author: SnuffleBag
replies.body:
>Its easy to make a game fully with AI.

It really isn't. This is why there currently exists exactly 0 good and/or commercially successful games fully made with AI.

It's easy to make something that gives the impression of being the promising beginnings of a game, and then lean on a crutch of "this was soo easy to make, imagine the potential" while never actually realizing said potential. Don't get fooled into thinking you can "just have AI make the game with a little human direction", AI is nowhere near at this level yet.

replies.author: fued
replies.body:
Its easy to make a game.
Its hard to make a good game.

That was my entire point.

replies.author: SnuffleBag
replies.body:
By that reasoning you could claim that creating a new template starter project is 'making a game', in which case it's also easy to make a game without AI ;)

It's not just about being a 'good game', but about being a high-quality production to expected industry standards. If AI could make a boring game with highly polished, coherent visuals, a perfectly balanced soundscape, great looking animations, responsive controls etc that would be one thing.. but it can't - all these sensationalist posts look like someone's first tutorial project, with the core focus being on how easy it was to make, not on how any part of it actually stands up to even the most basic scrutiny.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: It is common. And it makes a lot of people believe making games is now easy which leads to a lot of trash games. Don't fall in that trap. Use it as a tool to realize YOUR vision, don't as a creative lead.

replies.author: Able_Tell9927
replies.body: Thank you. I agree.

comments.author: tk_96f
comments.body:
It surely is but doesn't mean it allows you to have the excuses to cut short and be lazy about it. It still need YOU to lead and guide for a smooth development process, it's still a just tool after all.

I find it quite funny that those people asking the AI to build game in so called 'one shot, makers no mistake' approach is essentially equivalent to how your superior assigning you tasks WITHOUT giving you a clear instruction.

replies.author: Able_Tell9927
replies.body: I agree. Input = Output.

comments.author: Remote-Blackberry844
comments.body: Why can AAA games get away without listing AI but indies have to on steam

comments.author: SnuffleBag
comments.body: No, it's not common. It's common to use it for some select parts, but certainly not "almost all". You're asking in a very pro-AI channel, you should weight answers you get here against the same question cross-posted to a regular gamedev channel (which are generally quite anti-AI, but also generally more visited by people who have actually worked on and shipped commercial games).

comments.author: bigorangemachine
comments.body: AI will only get you so far
